gloss: catching all at once; sweeping roundup

definitions.gloss: catching all at once; sweeping roundup; rounding up everyone
definitions.explanation: Capturing or dealing with all members of a group in a single sweep. Originally from a Chinese idiom meaning to catch all fish in one cast of the net. Often used for police raids or decisive actions that eliminate an entire group at once.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}を{一網打尽|いちもうだじん}にする。
examples.english: To round up all the criminals at once.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{詐欺|さぎ}グループを{一網打尽|いちもうだじん}にした。
examples.english: The police rounded up the entire fraud ring.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{捜査|そうさ}の{末|すえ}、{密輸|みつゆ}{組織|そしき}を{一網打尽|いちもうだじん}にすることに{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: After years of investigation, they succeeded in rounding up the entire smuggling organization.

notes:
Four-character compound (yojijukugo): {一|いち} (one) + {網|もう} (net) + {打|だ} (strike) + {尽|じん} (exhaust, all). Literally "to exhaust with one cast of the net." From a Chinese historical anecdote.

USAGE:
Almost always used with にする in the pattern ～を{一網打尽|いちもうだじん}にする. Most commonly used in crime and law enforcement contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～を{一網打尽|いちもうだじん}にする (to round up ~ all at once)
- {一網打尽|いちもうだじん}に{捕|つか}まえる (to catch all at once)
